protocol: D-000 turn 3 of 3, same cycle as turns 1 and 2; not a fourth turn of CONTESTED D-099; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN scoped D-006 fleet-class successor plus RULE-GOVERNED naming of the v3 reserved G03/G04 identifiers
summary: Both accepted turn-2 findings are repaired correctly and the repair is confined to the repair. The hash/purge split is now explicit and structural rather than a sentence: full-file sha256(P) is taken before the purge that opens each cold/warm sequence and again after the pair completes, with stat of (st_dev, st_ino) — and an explicit 'Do not hash here' — occupying the one position between purge and cold exec where a data-page read would have manufactured a warm. I traced the ordering through both the first-release loop and the restructured second-release loop, including the per-command re-entry where step 1 hashes and step 2 purges: the hash always precedes the purge that clears it, so no hash ever warms the launch it guards. D101-T2-SF-1 is met by hoisting the check into a shared 'both platforms' block instead of leaving it macOS-only in preflight item 2. I did not review the macOS ISA derivation from the headers this turn; I compiled and ran it against MacOSX15.4.sdk, because the derivation is the load-bearing substitute for an API the entry says does not exist, and because my own D099-T3 suggestion died last turn from being reasoned rather than measured. Every conjunct holds. posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np is not merely a preference: requesting CPU_TYPE_X86_64 for a thin arm64 image and CPU_TYPE_ARM64 for a thin x86_64 image both fail the spawn outright with rc=86 EBADARCH, in both directions, so 'any other ISA is unspawnable' is measured rather than asserted. P_TRANSLATED performs the discrimination the entry assigns it: 0 for the native arm64 child, 1 for a live Rosetta x86_64 child, read from kinfo_proc.kp_proc.p_flag via KERN_PROC_PID on the target. I also re-ran the rejected route and reproduced turn 1 exactly — sysctl.proc_cputype resolved through MIB 0.102 with the PID appended returns 0x0100000c for self, for launchd, for the native child and for the Rosetta child whose P_TRANSLATED is 1 in the same run, so it restates the host CPU type and discriminates nothing. Most consequentially, I tested the absence claim I most expected to break the entry: PROC_PIDARCHINFO and struct proc_archinfo are present and unguarded in MacOSX26.5.sdk on this machine, which is exactly the shape of a stale rejection — but they are absent from the entire MacOSX15.4.sdk include tree, which is the SDK the entry scopes itself to and the one matching the macos-15 class. The scoping is what makes the claim true, and it is stated. All eight cited digests re-measure byte-exact, the five file-08 edit anchors each occur exactly once against the live register, PARTLY MET occurs exactly twice and both occurrences are covered, the freeze carries no condition-4 text to go stale, and the 18-of-18 numerator moves by exactly the two gates this entry names within D-086 rider RB-GHN-V3-A1's already-consented required-now denominator. Numerals stand, warm p50 is telemetry and cannot fail qualification, weekly rolls do not suppress the 10% rule, and nothing claims QUALIFIED, claims SATISFIED, names G13, restores G17, or moves condition 5. I have no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX.

notesNonBlocking.title: proc_pidpath returns the kernel-resolved path; step 3's equality needs P recorded resolved
notesNonBlocking.detail: macOS step 3 requires 'proc_pidpath(T) must equal P'. Measured: spawning /tmp/d101/child_arm64 returns /private/tmp/d101/child_arm64 (n=29). Any symlinked component in P — /tmp and $TMPDIR are symlinked on macOS — makes a naive string equality fail. The direction of failure is safe: the job is rejected and no measurement is admitted, so this cannot pass bad evidence. It is a false-reject robustness matter for the harness-authoring act, resolved by recording P as the realpath-normalized absolute path, which preflight item 2's 'Record absolute path P' already permits. Not blocking and not a defect in the decision.

notesNonBlocking.title: G04 governed-series cardinality is fixed only by the cross-reference to G03
notesNonBlocking.detail: G04 enumerates command x {steady baseline RSS, peak RSS} as 'one series of 21 samples', then adds cold/warm as a following sentence rather than as a dimension of the enumeration. The cardinality is nevertheless determined: 'Cold/warm applies to --help and --version RSS the same way as G03', and in G03 state is explicitly a series dimension, so G04 is 2 commands x 2 metrics x 2 states plus doctor read-only 1 x 2 x 1 = 10 governed series per platform. The paired 10% rule's 'For each G04 series' is well-defined once that is read through. Worth stating as a literal count in the harness rather than leaving it to the cross-reference, consistent with D101-T1-N-1 routing RSS methodology to harness authoring. Not blocking.

notesNonBlocking.title: The rejected sysctl route fails outright under the other invocation form
notesNonBlocking.detail: sysctl.proc_cputype lives in the CTL_SYSCTL name namespace and is not enumerated by sysctl -a (grep count 0 on this host). Passing the PID as newp to sysctlbyname fails outright; the documented form — sysctlnametomib giving MIB 0.102, then appending the PID and calling sysctl with miblen 3 — succeeds and returns the host CPU type. I hit the first form before the second and record it so the entry's 'returns the host CPU type' is not later mistaken for unreproducible: both forms support the rejection, one by returning a host-wide value and one by not answering at all. Turn 1's measurement reproduces exactly under the correct form.
notesNonBlocking.measured: MIB 0.102 + pid: 0x0100000c (ARM64) for self, launchd, thin-arm64 child, and Rosetta x86_64 child; the last has P_TRANSLATED=1 in the same run

notesNonBlocking.title: The 18 denominator excludes G06/G11/G13; that exclusion is inherited, not introduced here
notesNonBlocking.detail: Counted against the live register: 22 DR-G rows, 16 carrying a 'named:' harness prefix, 6 not (G03, G04, G06, G11, G13, G17). D-086 rider RB-GHN-V3-A1 fixes the required-now set at 18 with G17 dropped, G13 reserved behind DR-118, and G06/G11 BLOCKED by DR-002-008; D-088 wrote 16 of 18 on that basis with CONSENT from both reviewers at 0 MUST-FIX. D-101 names exactly G03 and G04 and moves the numerator by exactly 2, leaving the denominator untouched, so 18 of 18 is arithmetically correct within the already-consented frame. A reader who counts all 22 gate rows will still find three required-looking gates with no named harness; the register discloses this through '19 OPEN, 3 HARD-BLOCKED', the G17 inapplicability clause, and its own 'rows are authoritative' rule. Disclosure parity is preserved rather than reduced — the deleted fragment named G03/G04, which are precisely the two this entry names. Recording the boundary, not objecting to it.
notesNonBlocking.measured: 16 'named:' prefixes / 22 DR-G rows; 'PARTLY MET' occurs exactly 2x and both are covered by the edit list; '16 of 18' and 'remain required and unnamed' occur exactly 1x each

notesNonBlocking.title: The PROC_PIDARCHINFO rejection is SDK-version-scoped and an SDK bump reopens it
notesNonBlocking.detail: struct proc_archinfo and PROC_PIDARCHINFO (flavor 19) are present, public and unguarded in MacOSX26.5.sdk sys/proc_info.h at lines 352 and 766-767 on this machine, and absent from the whole MacOSX15.4.sdk include tree. The entry's rejection is therefore true only because it scopes itself to MacOSX15.4.sdk, which it states plainly and correctly ties to the macos-15 class rather than to the fleet-class definition. If the runner image or toolchain later moves to an SDK that exposes flavor 19, the 'no per-process CPU-type API exists' premise in step 5 stops holding and a simpler direct route becomes available. That is a successor trigger on the API-availability warrant, not on the class row, so it is not covered by the entry's existing successor-triggering list. Worth carrying forward; not a defect now.
notesNonBlocking.measured: grep of the full MacOSX15.4.sdk include tree for PROC_PIDARCHINFO: absent; MacOSX26.5.sdk: sys/proc_info.h:352, 766, 767
